key_results: 30.5% lower point-query latency vs. PGM-Index; 15.4% memory vs. K-D tree; Recall@10 improved 8.1% over best single-channel retriever; 12,420 QPS at 0.84 scaling efficiency
comments: Strong systems performance on real HEP/climate metadata, but evaluation limited to two scientific domains; generalization to other data modalities unclear.

outputs: query results (30.5% latency improvement), Recall@10 (8.1% gain)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Adaptive quantile quantization with z-order curves and incremental fine-tuning absorbs metadata distribution drift

hypotheses.hypothesis: Knowledge-graph-enhanced fusion outperforms static single-channel retrieval for scientific metadata
hypotheses.result: Supported; Recall@10 improved 8.1% over best single-channel baseline

title: Research on a CNC machine tool machining error analysis and prediction method based on digital twin and ISSLO-CNN

key_results: ISSLO-CNN achieved RMSE=3.84±0.16 μm, MAE=2.72±0.12 μm, R²=0.979±0.003; outperforms SSLO-CNN on physical consistency metrics; 1.97M parameters, 3.62 ms inference latency; ablation confirms both ISSLO improvements effective
comments: Strong prediction accuracy on NCMT-DT-Error dataset with practical inference efficiency, but closed-loop compensation performance untested; generalization to other CNC machines unknown.

model_io.model: ISSLO (improved stochastic social learning optimization with elite-guided adaptive learning factors and adaptive perturbation) tuning CNN hyperparameters

hypotheses.hypothesis: Elite-guided adaptive learning factors and adaptive perturbation strategy improve SSLO convergence efficiency and accuracy
hypotheses.result: Supported; ISSLO-CNN achieves superior RMSE, MAE, R² vs. SSLO-CNN; ablation confirms both improvements contribute

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multisource fused features (physical + virtual signals) enable accurate CNN-based error prediction without analytical aerodynamic modeling
hypotheses.result: Supported; RMSE 3.84 μm and R² 0.979 demonstrate practical prediction capability

key_results: RCSB-Net achieved 99.5% classification accuracy, 98.6% recall, 91.3% F1-score on LSS-FMCWR-1.0; 6.1 point improvement over ResNet-50

title: Electroglottographic and acoustic metrics of vocal technique in trained lyric sopranos: a descriptive cross-dataset study
task: Characterizing vocal technique in lyric sopranos via simultaneous electroglottographic and acoustic measurement
key_results: Breathy tone lower in CQ25, dEGG C/O ratio, CPP, HNR and higher in H1−H2 and shimmer; trill higher in EGG-jitter, F0 SD, modulation rate/extent; EGG-jitter–acoustic-jitter correlation r=0.864 pooled, r=0.575 median within-technique; random forest accuracy 0.961 (experimental→VocalSet), 0.889 (reverse transfer)
comments: Comprehensive multimodal dataset (1,104 valid tasks from 24 singers) with transparent descriptive statistics, but asymmetric cross-dataset transfer suggests singer and equipment effects dominate; singer-independent generalization not established.

model_io.model: Random forest classifier (trained on experimental EGG/acoustic features)
inputs: EGG (contact quotient, dEGG C/O ratio, jitter) and acoustic features (CPP, HNR, H1−H2, shimmer, F0 SD, modulation metrics) from 4 vocal techniques
outputs: technique classification (accuracy 0.961 on experimental holdout, 0.889 on VocalSet reverse transfer)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Breathy technique shows reduced glottal contact and acoustic periodicity markers vs. vibrato and trill
hypotheses.result: Supported; breathy tasks lower in CQ25, dEGG C/O ratio, CPP, HNR; higher in H1−H2 and shimmer

hypotheses.hypothesis: Trill represents intentional F0 modulation rather than cycle irregularity
hypotheses.result: Supported; trill shows elevated modulation rate/extent and F0 SD consistent with intended frequency variation, not jitter

hypotheses.hypothesis: EGG-jitter and acoustic jitter correlate strongly within singers
hypotheses.result: Supported; r=0.864 pooled, though within-technique medians r=0.575 suggest technique-specific variability

title: Sex-specific age prioritization of epidemic interventions under alternative equality objectives: a case study of COVID-19
task: Sex-specific age prioritization of COVID-19 interventions under alternative equality objectives
key_results: Male IFR at age X ≈ female IFR at age X+7; different equality objectives yield age thresholds differing by decades; Benefit/Mortality/Life-year Equality reduce vaccination thresholds by 3.49/4.92/6.62 and 3.12/3.75/4.47 years for males vs. females; total deaths change by −0.20%, +0.48%, +2.61% respectively vs. sex-neutral allocation
comments: Demonstrates how operational definitions of equity yield divergent priorities despite same underlying data; allocation outcomes depend critically on axiological choice, not epidemiology alone.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Male IFR at given age approximates female IFR ~7 years older
hypotheses.result: Supported; age-offset quantifies sex-specific mortality differences

hypotheses.hypothesis: Benefit/Mortality/Life-year Equality prioritization yields lower age thresholds for males vs. females and may increase total deaths vs. sex-neutral allocation
hypotheses.result: Supported; threshold reductions of 3.49–6.62 years for males; total death changes −0.20% to +2.61% depending on equality objective

title: Large electrocaloric effects in unannealed multilayer capacitors of partially ordered lead scandium tantalate
task: Achieve large electrocaloric effects in unannealed partially ordered lead scandium tantalate multilayers
key_results: Unannealed PbSc₀.₅Ta₀.₅O₃ (S₁₁₁~0.6) achieves |ΔTⱼ|~3.1 K vs 4.0 K for annealed (S₁₁₁~0.9–0.96); performance reduction only ~23% despite eliminating 42-day anneal
comments: High-field-induced ferroelectric phase compensates for reduced latent heat; eliminates expensive annealing without severely compromising cooler performance.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Partial B-site order and high-field-induced ferroelectricity preserve electrocaloric performance without annealing
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; unannealed multilayers retain 77% of annealed performance (3.1 K vs 4.0 K)

title: Electron dynamics in graphene irradiated by a quantum wave packet versus a classical point charge
task: Compare quantum wave packet vs classical point-charge descriptions of electron irradiation in graphene
key_results: At ~400 eV: quantum wave packet yields finite backscattering while classical ensemble predicts vanishing yield; wave-packet yield remains finite and decreases at higher energies
comments: Identifies experimentally accessible energy window (400 eV) to benchmark quantum vs classical electron descriptions; important for validating electron-beam nanofabrication models.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Quantum and classical electron descriptions diverge markedly at intermediate energies (400 eV)
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; quantum wave packet shows finite backscattering while classical vanishes
